answer.rationale: Two of the three current pressures (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are internal funnel issues that memory_31 and memory_86 directly address with a documented durable lift, so this is the lowest-risk, highest-leverage lever available this week. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but reacting with discounting risks a margin/race-to-bottom dynamic and may attract lower-quality, price-driven accounts that don't sustain qualified revenue long-term — exactly the kind of downstream value risk the objective warns against, so I want to verify the original memory_73 record before ever considering it, rather than acting on it now. I also want to verify memory_31 itself since it's the primary basis for this week's action and the record is old (day 12) relative to current conditions (competitor pressure, quarter-over-quarter decline) that could change its applicability. Given only one experiment slot and multiple confounded pressures happening simultaneously, I'm running this at standard_experiment scale rather than broad rollout, to confirm the lift still holds under current market conditions before committing further capacity, while flagging that even onboarding simplification carries some risk of admitting lower-intent signups that dilute downstream qualified revenue.
